title: Affine sheafification commutes with degreewise finite free signed duals
statement: Let Y be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], U an affine open, A=Γ(Y,U), and T the associated sheaf functor followed by transport from Spec A to U. Let K be any natural-indexed chain complex of A-modules whose every term is free and finitely generated. Put E=T(K extended into integer cochain degrees, with K_q in degree -q). Then D(E,O_U) [def-sc-signed-sheaf-dual-complex] is isomorphic as an integer cochain complex to T(D_A(K)) [def-sc-signed-module-dual-complex]. Neither boundedness nor Koszul regularity is assumed.

source.place: Tag 0BQZ, lemma-regular-immersion-ext, signed finite free Hom computation; https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0BQZ

proof.text: Choose the closed library basis Free.chooseBasis of each free finite term. Construct affineBasisSheafIso from the basis representation, tildeFinsupp and restriction of free sheaves. Construct affineBasisDualIso from the dual-basis representation and the closed homObjFreeUnitIso. These are actual isomorphism constructions, using no unproved theorem to supply data. Apply affineBasisDualIso_naturality to each chain boundary.

The private generic lemma signed_dual_iso_of_components assembles any natural family of term comparisons through an additive functor. In degree q≥0 conjugate each term comparison by mapIso of the canonical extendXIso for the chain extension at -q and the dual extension at q. In degree n<0 both terms are zero: use isZero_extend_X, map_isZero and the additive contravariant internal Hom functor to form the unique zero-object isomorphism.

For successive nonnegative degrees, extend_d_eq gives both differentials conjugated by their degree extension isomorphisms. The scalar identity (-1)^(q+1)=-(-1)^q is proved by ModuleCat.hom_ext, and map_units_smul transports it through the additive functor. Functoriality and inverse identities cancel the extension maps; naturality of the term comparison gives the remaining equation. For negative source degree, every composite from its zero object is equal. HomologicalComplex.Hom.isoOfComponents produces the required complex isomorphism.
